query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: The trend in the research is to improve the mechanical performance of magnetic-refrigeration materials while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect. This has been attempted through various methods such as alloying, microstructural optimization, and thermomechanical processing. High-entropy alloys have shown promise in achieving a balance between magnetic and mechanical properties. Recent studies have focused on tuning the microstructure and composition of these alloys to enhance their performance.
decision.unsolved: The unsolved problem is to find a single intervention that can improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect. decision.why: Thermomechanical processing has been shown to be effective in improving the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys while retaining their magnetic properties. By applying this technique to MnNiSi-based materials, it may be possible to achieve the desired balance between mechanical performance and magnetocaloric effect.
